llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (manage skills from a GitHub-backed repo) matches most of its behavior, but the runtime instructions ask the agent to read other local config files for tokens, overwrite local skill files from upstream, and perform git push operations using a GitHub token — actions that are powerful and not fully constrained or justified in the SKILL.md.

dimensions.detail: The skill is a GitHub-backed skill manager, so requiring git, a GitHub token, and a config path (~/.anyskill/config.json) is coherent. However, the SKILL.md also references reading other local environment stores (e.g., mentions ~/.openclaw/.env) for tokens and will write/commit changes into user repositories — these are more powerful than a read-only index/search tool and should be clearly justified.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions direct the agent to search multiple config locations, read tokens from env/config, fetch raw files from raw.githubusercontent.com, overwrite local SKILL.md and infra files, and run git commit/push. It also auto-re-clones a repo if localPath is missing. The SKILL.md potentially reads unrelated files (mentions ~.openclaw/.env) and dynamically loads/overwrites skill instructions from a remote source — granting the remote repo the ability to change agent behavior. Those actions go beyond passive indexing and introduce write/execute-side effects on the filesystem and remote repos.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec, which minimizes installation risk. It relies on existing git on PATH; no downloads or archive extraction are performed by an install step in the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires a single GitHub token (ANYSKILL_GITHUB_TOKEN), which is appropriate in principle. But the SKILL.md expects to use that token for cloning and pushing to the user's repo (potentially requiring broad repo permissions). The instructions also state token discovery may look in other files (e.g., ~/.openclaw/.env), which is outside the declared requires.env and is unnecessary for the skill's basic GitHub integration — this is scope creep and increases the chance of credential exposure. The skill does not specify required token scopes (read-only vs read/write).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true. It will write configuration at ~/.anyskill/config.json and will write, overwrite, commit, and push files in the user's target repository when updating infra or SKILL.md (after prompting). Because the skill can dynamically overwrite its own SKILL.md and other repo files from upstream, it grants the remote repo the ability to change agent behavior; combined with an agent that can invoke skills autonomously, that increases risk if the upstream is untrusted.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent with a GitHub-backed skill manager, but it performs powerful write actions and token discovery beyond a simple read-only index. Before installing: 1) Only provide a dedicated GitHub PAT with minimal scope (ideally repo-scoped and limited to the specific repository), not your global or org-wide token. 2) Inspect the upstream repository (https://github.com/lanyijianke/AnySkill) and confirm you trust its contents because the skill will fetch and overwrite SKILL.md and infra files from that upstream. 3) Be aware the skill may commit and push changes to your repository; if you want only read/search behavior, avoid giving push permissions. 4) The SKILL.md references scanning other local env/config files (e.g., ~/.openclaw/.env) — if you don’t want the skill to look for tokens in other places, do not provide a token and place a config in ~/.anyskill/config.json that contains only the allowed repo/localPath. 5) Consider running the skill in a restricted environment or using a narrowly-scoped token and review any commits the skill proposes before pushing. If you want, supply the full SKILL.md and the rest of the truncated sections so I can re-evaluate specifics (e.g., exact token discovery locations and confirmation prompts).
